definition_zh: 南方的；南部的；南方特有的
definition_en: in or from the south, or typical of the south
core_image: 地图上温暖的南部海岸线，阳光与棕榈树
scene: 这座南方城市冬天很温暖。This southern city is warm in winter.
sceneCN: 这里 southern 是「南方的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座南方城市冬天很温暖。

senses.title: Of the south
senses.definition: located in or belonging to the south
senses.definitionCN: 位于或属于南方的
senses.example: This southern city is warm in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座南方城市冬天很温暖。
senses.why: This is the basic directional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的方位含义。

senses.title: Of a southern region
senses.definition: in the southern part of a particular country
senses.definitionCN: 位于某个国家南部的
senses.example: The southern border is guarded.
senses.exampleCN: 南部边界有人守卫。
senses.why: A region gives the direction a local name.
senses.whyCN: 地区给方向一个本地的名字。

senses.title: Typical of the south
senses.definition: characteristic of the south, such as its weather or speech
senses.definitionCN: 具有南方特征的，如气候或口音
senses.example: She speaks with a southern accent.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话带南方口音。
senses.why: Place shapes manner, and the adjective records it.
senses.whyCN: 地方塑造风格，形容词记录了这种风格。

intro.en: Southern is south with an old adjective ending.
intro.cn: southern 是 south 加一个古老的形容词词尾。

items.en: Sutherne meant of the south.
items.cn: sutherne 意为南方的。

items.en: The form became southerne.
items.cn: 词形变为 southerne。

items.en: Southern named regions and their weather.
items.cn: southern 指地区及其气候。

items.en: It also named accents and customs.
items.cn: 它也指口音与习俗。

items.en: Southern Hemisphere fixed it in geography.
items.cn: Southern Hemisphere 把它固定在地理用语中。

note.en: Southern is compared with the other compass adjectives.
note.cn: 把 southern 与其他方位形容词作比较。

entries.definition: of the hot regions near the equator

normalIntro.en: Southern puts the south in front of a noun.
normalIntro.cn: southern 把「南方」放在名词前面。

normal.en: This southern city is warm in winter.
normal.cn: 这座南方城市冬天很温暖。

normal.en: The southern border is guarded.
She speaks with a southern accent.
The southern coast is full of small bays.
Penguins live in the Southern Hemisphere.

abstract.en: Southern is a direction wearing local clothes.
abstract.cn: southern 是穿上地方衣裳的方向。

abstract.en: The south is warm in weather and in memory.
abstract.cn: 南方在天气里温暖，在记忆里也温暖。

abstract.en: Every region makes its own version of the same word.
abstract.cn: 每个地区都为同一个词造出自己的版本。

examples.en: This southern city is warm in winter.
examples.cn: 这座南方城市冬天很温暖。

examples.en: The southern border is guarded.
examples.cn: 南部边界有人守卫。

examples.en: She speaks with a southern accent.
examples.cn: 她说话带南方口音。

dict_mnemonic.text: southern 由 south 加 -ern 构成，类似 northern、eastern、western；southern part 是「南部」，Southern Hemisphere 是「南半球」，southern accent 是「南方口音」。

root: 来自古英语 sutherne（南方的），由 south 加形容词词尾构成，核心义为方位上的南方及其地方特征。

sensesIntro.en: Southern means of the south, of a southern region, or typical of the south.
sensesIntro.cn: southern 意为南方的、南部地区的，或具有南方特征的。

core.en: The south attached to a place or thing.
core.cn: 附着在地方或事物上的「南方」。

branches.en: A warm city sits low on the map.
branches.cn: 一座温暖的城市位于地图下方。

branches.en: A line is drawn along the lower border.
branches.cn: 一条线沿着南部边界画出。

branches.en: A voice carries a soft local music.
branches.cn: 一个嗓音带着柔和的地方音调。

branches.en: Direction becomes region when it is named.
branches.cn: 方向被命名，就成了地区。

branches.en: A place shapes both its border and its speech.
branches.cn: 一个地方既塑造边界，也塑造言语。

intro.en: Southern joins south with the adjective ending -ern.
intro.cn: southern 由 south 加形容词词尾 -ern 构成。

latinIntro.en: Southern is Germanic; Latin has no matching root.
latinIntro.cn: southern 属日耳曼语，拉丁语没有对应的词根。

items.example: The swallows fly south in winter.
This southern city is warm in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这座南方城市冬天很温暖。

definition_en: an empty area, the region beyond the earth, or a gap between things
core_image: 空旷的房间里，阳光从高窗斜射进来，地上留出大片空地
scene: 这间屋子需要更多空间。This room needs more space.
sceneCN: 这里 space 是「空间」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这间屋子需要更多空间。

senses.title: Empty area
senses.definition: an area that is empty and available
senses.definitionCN: 空旷可用的区域
senses.example: This room needs more space.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子需要更多空间。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of room to move or put things.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示活动或放置余地的含义。

senses.title: Beyond the earth
senses.definition: the region beyond the earth's atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 地球大气层以外的区域
senses.example: The rocket rose into space.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭升入太空。
senses.why: The greatest empty area we know took the same word.
senses.whyCN: 我们所知最大的空旷区域，用了同一个词。

senses.title: A gap
senses.definition: an empty distance or place between things
senses.definitionCN: 事物之间的空距或空位
senses.example: Leave a space between the lines.
senses.exampleCN: 行与行之间留出间隔。
senses.why: A gap is empty area on a smaller scale.
senses.whyCN: 间隙是更小尺度上的空余区域。

intro.en: Space came from Latin through French, meaning an extent or room.
intro.cn: space 从拉丁语经法语而来，意为范围或余地。

items.en: Spatium meant an area, a distance, or a period.
items.cn: spatium 意为区域、距离或一段时间。

items.en: Espace named an extent or room.
items.cn: espace 指范围或余地。

items.en: Space entered English as room or extent.
items.cn: space 作为余地或范围进入英语。

items.en: It named the gap between written words.
items.cn: 它指书写词语之间的间隔。

items.en: Outer space extended it beyond the sky.
items.cn: outer space 把它扩展到天空之外。

note.en: Space is compared with look-alike words and words for room.
note.cn: 把 space 与形近词以及表示空间的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Space is the emptiness that makes room for things.
normalIntro.cn: space 是为事物腾出余地的空无。

normal.en: This room needs more space.
normal.cn: 这间屋子需要更多空间。

normal.en: The rocket rose into space.
Leave a space between the lines.
The car found a parking space.
normal.cn: 汽车找到了一个停车位。

normal.en: Stars fill the vast space of the night.
normal.cn: 星星布满夜晚辽阔的太空。

abstract.en: Space is what silence is made of.
abstract.cn: 空间，是沉默的构成材料。

abstract.en: Without empty room, nothing can move.
abstract.cn: 没有空白余地，万物都无法移动。

abstract.en: The mind needs space as much as a room does.
abstract.cn: 心智需要空间，不亚于房间。

examples.en: This room needs more space.
examples.cn: 这间屋子需要更多空间。

examples.en: The rocket rose into space.
examples.cn: 火箭升入太空。

examples.en: Leave a space between the lines.
examples.cn: 行与行之间留出间隔。

dict_mnemonic.text: space 是空间、太空，spacious 是「宽敞的」，spacing 是「间距」；outer space 是「外层空间」，space station 是「空间站」，parking space 是「停车位」。

root: 来自拉丁语 spatium（区域、距离、时段），经古法语 espace 进入英语，核心义为空余的范围，后扩展为太空。

sensesIntro.en: Space means an empty area, the region beyond the earth, or a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: space 指空余的区域、地球之外的太空，或事物之间的间隔。

core.en: Emptiness measured for use.
core.cn: 为使用而丈量的空。

branches.en: Sunlight fills a bare room.
branches.cn: 阳光充满一间空旷的屋子。

branches.en: A rocket crosses the dark sky.
branches.cn: 一枚火箭划过黑暗的天空。

branches.en: Two words stand apart on a line.
branches.cn: 两个词在纸面上分开站立。

branches.en: The room and the universe are both empty and open.
branches.cn: 房间与宇宙，都是空而开放的。

branches.en: Great and small emptiness share one name.
branches.cn: 大小不同的空，共用一个名字。

intro.en: Space forms adjectives, nouns, and compounds.
intro.cn: space 构成形容词、名词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is spatium, an extent or area.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 spatium，意为范围或区域。

items.exampleCN: 这间屋子需要更多空间。

items.example: The hall has many open spaces.
items.exampleCN: 大厅里有许多开阔的空间。

items.example: They live in a spacious flat.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一套宽敞的公寓里。

items.example: The spacing of the chairs is even.

items.exampleCN: 保持你的工作空间整洁。
飞机进入了我们的领空。

definition_en: to give time or money, to save, to forgive, or kept as extra
core_image: 柜子里放着一把备用钥匙，静静等着需要它的那天
scene: 你能抽出几分钟吗？Can you spare a few minutes?
sceneCN: 这里 spare 是「抽出」（第 1 个义项）；句意：你能抽出几分钟吗？

senses.title: To give time or resources
senses.definition: to be able to give time, money, or effort to someone
senses.definitionCN: 能够把时间、金钱或精力分给别人
senses.example: Can you spare a few minutes?
senses.exampleCN: 你能抽出几分钟吗？
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of making room for others.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示为他人腾出余地的含义。

senses.title: To forgive
senses.definition: to choose not to harm or punish someone
senses.definitionCN: 选择不伤害或惩罚某人
senses.example: The king spared the prisoner.
senses.exampleCN: 国王饶了那个囚犯。
senses.why: To spare is to hold back the blow.
senses.whyCN: 饶恕，就是把打击收住。

senses.title: Kept as extra
senses.definition: kept in addition in case it is needed
senses.definitionCN: 额外保留以备需要
senses.example: We keep a spare key under the mat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在垫子下放了一把备用钥匙。
senses.why: What is set aside is being spared for later.
senses.whyCN: 被留出来的东西，就是为以后省下的。

intro.en: Spare first meant to hold back from harming.
intro.cn: spare 最初意为克制不去伤害。

items.en: Sparian meant to refrain from harming or using.
items.cn: sparian 意为不伤害或不使用。

items.en: The form became spare and kept mercy.
items.cn: 词形变为 spare，保留宽恕之义。

items.en: It came to mean to save or set aside.
items.cn: 它开始表示节省或留出。

items.en: The adjective named what is kept extra.
items.cn: 形容词指额外保留的东西。

items.en: Phrases like spare time fixed the modern uses.
items.cn: spare time 等短语固定了现代用法。

note.en: Spare is compared with look-alike words and words for saving.
note.cn: 把 spare 与形近词以及表示节省、宽恕的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To spare is to loosen your hold on something for someone else.
normalIntro.cn: spare 是为别人放松对某物的握持。

normal.en: Can you spare a few minutes?
The king spared the prisoner.
We keep a spare key under the mat.
normal.cn: 我们在垫子下放了一把备用钥匙。

normal.en: He spares no effort in his work.
Spare a thought for those who are cold.
normal.cn: 体谅一下那些受冻的人。

abstract.en: Spare is a word that makes room for mercy.
abstract.cn: spare 是一个为宽恕腾出空间的词。

abstract.en: What we spare, we still care for.
abstract.cn: 我们饶过的东西，说明我们仍在意。

abstract.en: A spare minute is a gift with no wrapping.
abstract.cn: 空出的一分钟，是一份没有包装的礼物。

examples.en: Can you spare a few minutes?
examples.cn: 你能抽出几分钟吗？

examples.en: The king spared the prisoner.
examples.cn: 国王饶了那个囚犯。

examples.en: We keep a spare key under the mat.
examples.cn: 我们在垫子下放了一把备用钥匙。

dict_mnemonic.text: spare 既是动词也是形容词；spare time 是「空闲时间」，spare no effort 是「不遗余力」，spare key 是「备用钥匙」，sparingly 是「节省地」。

root: 来自古英语 sparian（不伤害、不使用），核心义为克制与保留，后分化为抽出、饶恕与备用。

sensesIntro.en: Spare means to give time or resources, to forgive, or to keep something extra.
sensesIntro.cn: spare 指抽出时间或资源、饶恕他人，或保留备用的东西。

core.en: Holding back what could be used or given.
core.cn: 对本可使用或给予之物的克制。

branches.en: A busy person pauses to listen.
branches.cn: 忙碌的人停下来倾听。

branches.en: A hand is raised to strike but stops.
branches.cn: 举起来要打的手停住了。

branches.en: A spare key waits under a mat.
branches.cn: 一把备用钥匙等在垫子下。

branches.en: Giving time and giving mercy are both letting go.
branches.cn: 给出时间与给出宽恕，都是放手。

branches.en: What is spared is kept for a future need.
branches.cn: 被饶过或保留的，是留给未来需要的。

intro.en: Spare forms a verb paradigm and two derived modifiers.
intro.cn: spare 构成动词变化形式和两个派生修饰词。

latinIntro.en: Spare has no Latin root; it comes from Old English sparian.
latinIntro.cn: spare 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 sparian。

items.example: Can you spare a few minutes?
He is sparing with his words.

items.exampleCN: 这个房间布置得很简朴。

items.example: The spareness of the design pleased her.
He was unsparing in his criticism.

definition_en: to say words, to give a speech, or to use a language
core_image: 母亲俯身对孩子轻声说话，孩子仰头认真听着
scene: 她轻声对孩子们说话。She spoke softly to the children.
sceneCN: 这里 speak 是「说话」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她轻声对孩子们说话。

senses.title: To say words
senses.definition: to say words with your voice
senses.definitionCN: 用嗓音说出词语
senses.example: She spoke softly to the children.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻声对孩子们说话。
senses.why: This is the basic everyday sense of using the voice.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常使用嗓音说话的基本含义。

senses.title: To address an audience
senses.definition: to give a formal talk to a group
senses.definitionCN: 向一群人作正式讲话
senses.example: She spoke at the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会议上发了言。
senses.why: Speaking to many people became a formal act with its own sense.
senses.whyCN: 对众人讲话成为一种正式行为，因而单列一义。

senses.title: To use a language
senses.definition: to be able to use a particular language
senses.definitionCN: 能够使用某种语言
senses.example: Do you speak French?
senses.exampleCN: 你讲法语吗？
senses.why: Knowing a language is shown by speaking it.
senses.whyCN: 掌握一门语言，正体现在能说这门语言。

intro.en: Speak comes from an old English verb meaning to say or talk.
intro.cn: speak 来自古英语中表示说或谈的动词。

items.en: Specan meant to speak or talk.
items.cn: specan 意为说话或交谈。

items.en: The verb became speken and kept its meaning.
items.cn: 动词变为 speken，含义不变。

items.en: The past forms became spoke and spoken.
items.cn: 过去式与过去分词定为 spoke 和 spoken。

items.en: To speak at an event meant to give a formal talk.
items.cn: 在活动中 speak 表示作正式发言。

items.en: To speak a language meant to command it in speech.
items.cn: speak a language 表示能够在口头使用该语言。

note.en: Speak is compared with look-alike words and other verbs of saying.
note.cn: 把 speak 与形近词以及其他表示说的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Speak is the act of putting words into the air.
normalIntro.cn: speak 是把词语送进空气里的动作。

normal.en: She spoke softly to the children.
She spoke at the conference.
Do you speak French?
Please speak up so everyone can hear.
normal.cn: 请大声说，让大家都能听见。

normal.en: He spoke for the whole team.

abstract.en: To speak is to hand a thought across the air.
abstract.cn: 说话，就是把念头递过空气。

abstract.en: Words spoken cannot be taken back.
abstract.cn: 说出口的话收不回来。

abstract.en: A language lives only while someone speaks it.
abstract.cn: 一门语言只在有人讲它时活着。

examples.en: She spoke softly to the children.
examples.cn: 她轻声对孩子们说话。

examples.en: She spoke at the conference.
examples.cn: 她在会议上发了言。

examples.en: Do you speak French?
examples.cn: 你讲法语吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: speak 是说话，speaker 是「说话者、扬声器」，speech 是「演讲、言语」；speak up 是「大声说」，speak out 是「公开表态」，speak for 是「代表发言」。

root: 来自古英语 specan（说、谈），属日耳曼语族，与 speech 同源，核心义为用嗓音发出有意义的词语。

sensesIntro.en: Speak means to say words, to address a group, or to use a language.
sensesIntro.cn: speak 指说出词语、向众人发言，或使用某种语言。

core.en: Voice turned into meaning.
core.cn: 嗓音化为意义。

branches.en: A mother murmurs to her child.
branches.cn: 母亲对孩子低声细语。

branches.en: A figure stands before a hall of listeners.
branches.cn: 一个人站在满堂听众面前。

branches.en: Two strangers greet each other in a second tongue.
branches.cn: 两个陌生人用第二语言互相问候。

branches.en: Quiet talk and public address both use the same voice.
branches.cn: 私语与演说使用同一个嗓音。

branches.en: Mastering a language lets you speak before any audience.
branches.cn: 掌握一门语言，就能在任何听众前发言。

intro.en: Speak forms nouns for people and for the act of speaking.
intro.cn: speak 构成表示人和说话行为的名词。

latinIntro.en: Speak is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: speak 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: She spoke softly to the children.
The words were spoken in anger.
items.exampleCN: 那些话是在气头上说的。

items.example: She is speaking on the phone.
The speaker was easy to hear.
items.exampleCN: 发言人的声音很容易听清。
他作了一个简短的演讲。

definition_zh: 特别的；专门的；特色菜（或特价品）
definition_en: different from the usual, intended for one purpose, or a dish offered on a particular day
core_image: 餐桌上点着蜡烛，摆着一份与平日不同的精致晚餐
scene: 今天是个特别的日子。Today is a special day.
sceneCN: 这里 special 是「特别的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：今天是个特别的日子。

senses.title: Out of the ordinary
senses.definition: better or different from what is usual
senses.definitionCN: 比寻常更好或与寻常不同的
senses.example: Today is a special day.
senses.exampleCN: 今天是个特别的日子。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of something set apart from the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示某事物不同于寻常的含义。

senses.title: For one purpose
senses.definition: designed or intended for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一特定目的设计或准备的
senses.example: The school has special classes for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为初学者开设了专门的课程。
senses.why: Something set apart for one purpose is special in a practical sense.
senses.whyCN: 为某一目的单独分出的事物，在实用意义上就是专门的。

senses.title: A dish of the day
senses.definition: a dish or item offered on a particular day at a reduced price
senses.definitionCN: 某日特别供应或降价的菜品、商品
senses.example: Today's special is fish soup.
senses.exampleCN: 今天的特色菜是鱼汤。
senses.why: A dish singled out for the day is literally a special.
senses.whyCN: 当日被单独挑出的菜品，字面上就是 special。

intro.en: Special came from Latin through French, meaning of a particular kind.
intro.cn: special 从拉丁语经法语而来，意为属于某一特定种类的。

items.en: Specialis meant belonging to a particular kind.
items.cn: specialis 意为属于某一特定种类的。

items.en: Especial named something distinct or exceptional.
items.cn: especial 指独特或例外的事物。

items.en: Special entered English with the same sense.
items.cn: special 带着同样的含义进入英语。

items.en: It came to mean dear or beloved as well.
items.cn: 它也曾表示珍爱的、心爱的。

items.en: A dish of the day was called the special.
items.cn: 当日的特色菜被称为 the special。

note.en: Special is compared with look-alike words and words for the unusual.
note.cn: 把 special 与形近词以及表示不寻常的词作比较。

entries.definition: the only one of its kind

normalIntro.en: Special marks whatever is singled out from the ordinary.
normalIntro.cn: special 标记从寻常中被单独挑出的事物。

normal.en: Today is a special day.
The school has special classes for beginners.
normal.cn: 学校为初学者开设了专门的课程。

normal.en: Today's special is fish soup.
They gave her special attention.
The shop has a special offer this week.
normal.cn: 这家店本周有特价优惠。

abstract.en: Special is what memory keeps when the rest fades.
abstract.cn: 其余的都淡去了，记忆留下的就是特别。

abstract.en: A day becomes special because someone chose it.
abstract.cn: 日子之所以特别，是因为有人选择了它。

abstract.en: To call a thing special is to set it apart with words.
abstract.cn: 称一物特别，就是用言语把它单独挑出。

examples.en: Today is a special day.
examples.cn: 今天是个特别的日子。

examples.en: The school has special classes for beginners.
examples.cn: 学校为初学者开设了专门的课程。

examples.en: Today's special is fish soup.
examples.cn: 今天的特色菜是鱼汤。

dict_mnemonic.text: special 是「特别的、专门的」，也可作名词指「特色菜、特价品」；specially 是「专门地」，specialty 是「特产、专长」，specialist 是「专家」，specialize 是「专攻」。

root: 来自拉丁语 specialis（属于某一特定种类的），源于 species（种类、外观），核心义为从同类中单独挑出的、特别的。

sensesIntro.en: Special means unusual, intended for one purpose, or a dish singled out for the day.
sensesIntro.cn: special 指非同寻常的、为特定目的准备的，或当日特别供应的菜品。

core.en: Set apart from the rest of its kind.
core.cn: 从同类中被单独分出。

branches.en: A candlelit table stands out from every other night.
branches.cn: 烛光餐桌在每个寻常夜晚中格外显眼。

branches.en: One class is kept for those who are new.
branches.cn: 有一个班专为初学者保留。

branches.en: The cook sets aside one dish for today.
branches.cn: 厨师为今天单独留出一道菜。

branches.en: Both the unusual and the purpose-built are set apart.
branches.cn: 与众不同与专用安排，都是被单独分出。

branches.en: A special class and a special dish are each singled out for a use.
branches.cn: 专门的班级与特供的菜品，都因用途被挑出。

intro.en: Special forms adverbs, nouns, and verbs of focusing.
intro.cn: special 构成副词、名词和表示专注的动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is species, a kind or appearance, and specialis, of a kind.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 species（种类、外观）和 specialis（属于某一种类的）。

items.example: The cake was specially made for her.
items.exampleCN: 这蛋糕是专门为她做的。

items.example: Fish soup is the house specialty.
He paid especial attention to detail.

items.exampleCN: 她的拿手甜点是苹果派。

definition_en: a formal talk given to an audience, or the ability to speak and the words used
core_image: 讲台上一盏台灯照亮演讲稿，台下是一排排安静聆听的面孔
scene: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
sceneCN: 这里 speech 是「演讲」（第 1 个义项）；句意：校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。

senses.title: A formal talk
senses.definition: a formal talk given to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 向听众作的正式讲话
senses.example: The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。
senses.why: This is the most familiar modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最熟悉的含义。

senses.title: The power to speak
senses.definition: the ability to speak, or the act of speaking
senses.definitionCN: 说话的能力或行为
senses.example: Speech develops early in children.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童很早就发展出说话能力。
senses.why: The older sense names the human power itself.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的含义指人类说话的能力本身。

senses.title: Words that are spoken
senses.definition: the words people use and the way they speak
senses.definitionCN: 人们使用的言语及其表达方式
senses.example: The law limits hate speech.
senses.exampleCN: 法律限制仇恨言论。
senses.why: The content of speaking became a public matter.
senses.whyCN: 说话的内容成为公共事务。

intro.en: Speech is an old English word for speaking, related to speak.
intro.cn: speech 是古英语中表示说话的词，与 speak 同源。

items.en: Spræc meant speech, language, or a saying.
items.cn: spræc 意为言语、语言或说法。

items.en: The form became speche.
items.cn: 词形变为 speche。

items.en: Speech named both the power and a formal address.
items.cn: speech 同时指说话能力和正式讲话。

items.en: Freedom of speech made it a political word.
items.cn: freedom of speech 使它成为政治词汇。

items.en: Part of speech named word classes in grammar.
items.cn: part of speech 成为语法中的词类术语。

note.en: Speech is compared with look-alike words and words for talks.
note.cn: 把 speech 与形近词以及表示讲话的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Speech is speaking made public, or the power that makes it possible.
normalIntro.cn: speech 是被公开的说话，或让说话成为可能的能力。

normal.en: The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
normal.cn: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。

normal.en: Speech develops early in children.
normal.cn: 儿童很早就发展出说话能力。

normal.en: The law limits hate speech.
She wrote her speech the night before.
normal.cn: 她前一天晚上写了演讲稿。

normal.en: Freedom of speech is protected by law.

abstract.en: Speech is thought given a body of air.
abstract.cn: 言语是给思想一副空气的身体。

abstract.en: A speech ends, but its echo keeps working.
abstract.cn: 演讲会结束，回声却继续工作。

abstract.en: The right to speak belongs even to those we dislike.
abstract.cn: 说话的权利，也属于我们不喜欢的人。

examples.en: The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
examples.cn: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。

examples.en: Speech develops early in children.
examples.cn: 儿童很早就发展出说话能力。

examples.en: The law limits hate speech.
examples.cn: 法律限制仇恨言论。

dict_mnemonic.text: speech 是古英语 spræc 演变而来，与 speak 同源，指「演讲、言语」；give a speech 是「发表演讲」，freedom of speech 是「言论自由」，part of speech 是「词性」，speechless 是「说不出话的」。

root: 来自古英语 spræc（言语、说话），与 speak 同源，属日耳曼语族，核心义为用词语表达的行为及其公开形式。

sensesIntro.en: Speech means a formal talk, the power to speak, or the words people use.
sensesIntro.cn: speech 指正式演讲、说话能力，或人们使用的言语。

core.en: Words carried into the air for others.
core.cn: 被送进空气、传给别人的词语。

branches.en: A speaker stands before a hall of graduates.
branches.cn: 演讲者站在满堂毕业生面前。

branches.en: A small child forms a first clear sentence.
branches.cn: 小孩说出第一个清晰的句子。

branches.en: A law draws a line around what may be said.
branches.cn: 一条法律为可说的话划出界线。

branches.en: A public address rests on the human power to speak.
branches.cn: 公开演说依赖于人类说话的能力。

branches.en: The ability and its content both carry the name.
branches.cn: 能力与其内容都带着同一个名字。

intro.en: Speech connects to the whole speaking family.
intro.cn: speech 与整个说话词族相连。

latinIntro.en: Speech is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: speech 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
items.exampleCN: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。

items.example: He stared speechlessly at the letter.
She spoke softly to the children.
The speaker walked to the podium.
She is speaking on the phone.

items.exampleCN: 战争带来了难以言表的苦难。

definition_en: how fast something moves, the quality of being fast, or to move or make something move faster
core_image: 汽车在空旷的公路上越开越快，路边的标牌向后飞掠成一片模糊
scene: 汽车在高速公路上加速。The car gathered speed on the highway.
sceneCN: 这里 speed 是「速度」（第 1 个义项）；句意：汽车在高速公路上加速。

senses.title: Rate of movement
senses.definition: the rate at which something moves
senses.definitionCN: 某物移动的速率
senses.example: The car gathered speed on the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在高速公路上加速。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词核心的物理含义。

senses.title: The quality of being fast
senses.definition: the quality of moving or acting quickly
senses.definitionCN: 移动或行动迅速的性质
senses.example: She finished the work with great speed.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常迅速地完成了工作。
senses.why: Speed also names quickness itself, not only a number.
senses.whyCN: speed 也指迅速本身，而不只是一个数值。

senses.title: To move fast
senses.definition: to move quickly, or to make something move faster
senses.definitionCN: 快速移动，或使某物移动得更快
senses.example: He sped away on his bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。
senses.why: The verb turns the quality into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这种性质变成动作。

intro.en: Speed first meant success, then quickness, then rate of movement.
intro.cn: speed 最初意为成功，后指迅速，再指移动的速度。

items.en: Sped meant success or prosperity.
items.cn: sped 意为成功或兴旺。

items.en: The word came to mean quickness, as success came fast.
items.cn: 由于成功来得快，这个词开始表示迅速。

items.en: Speed came to mean the rate of motion.
items.cn: speed 开始表示运动的速率。

items.en: Speed limit gave it a legal sense.
items.cn: speed limit 赋予它法律含义。

items.en: To speed up became the common verb of hurrying.
items.cn: speed up 成为常用的催促动词。

note.en: Speed is compared with look-alike words and words for rate.
note.cn: 把 speed 与形近词以及表示速率的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Speed measures how quickly distance is crossed.
normalIntro.cn: speed 衡量距离被越过得多快。

normal.en: The car gathered speed on the highway.
normal.cn: 汽车在高速公路上加速。

normal.en: She finished the work with great speed.
normal.cn: 她非常迅速地完成了工作。

normal.en: He sped away on his bike.
normal.cn: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。

normal.en: The speed limit here is low.
The train reached its top speed.

abstract.en: Speed compresses time into distance.
abstract.cn: 速度把时间压缩成距离。

abstract.en: The faster we move, the less we see.
abstract.cn: 移动得越快，看见的越少。

abstract.en: Hurry is speed without direction.
abstract.cn: 匆忙是没有方向的速度。

examples.en: The car gathered speed on the highway.
examples.cn: 汽车在高速公路上加速。

examples.en: She finished the work with great speed.
examples.cn: 她非常迅速地完成了工作。

examples.en: He sped away on his bike.
examples.cn: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。

dict_mnemonic.text: speed 是「速度、快速」，也可作动词表示「加速」；speed limit 是「限速」，speed up 是「加速」，speedy 是「迅速的」，speedometer 是「速度计」。

root: 来自古英语 sped（成功、顺利），因成功常来得迅速而引申为快速，再指移动速率，动词义为加速、疾驰。

sensesIntro.en: Speed means the rate of movement, quickness, or to move faster.
sensesIntro.cn: speed 指移动速率、迅速，或表示加速。

core.en: Distance divided by the time it takes.
core.cn: 距离除以所花的时间。

branches.en: A car pushes faster along an open road.
branches.cn: 汽车在开阔公路上越开越快。

branches.en: Hands finish a task before the clock expects.
branches.cn: 双手比时钟预料的更早完成任务。

branches.en: A bicycle rushes past a gate.
branches.cn: 一辆自行车冲过门口。

branches.en: The measure and the hurrying act share one word.
branches.cn: 度量与疾驰的动作共用一个词。

branches.en: Quickness in work and movement both look like speed.
branches.cn: 工作与移动中的迅速都像速度。

intro.en: Speed forms adjectives, adverbs, and measuring devices.
intro.cn: speed 构成形容词、副词和测量装置。

latinIntro.en: Speed is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: speed 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The car gathered speed on the highway.
items.exampleCN: 汽车在高速公路上加速。

items.example: The two cars reached different speeds.
items.exampleCN: 两辆车达到了不同的速度。

items.example: He sped away on his bike.
items.exampleCN: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。

items.example: They wished her a speedy recovery.
The race was held on a speedway.
items.exampleCN: 比赛在赛车跑道上举行。

definition_en: to write or say the letters of a word in order, or to mean something in a serious way
core_image: 孩子用手指在沙盘上一个字母一个字母地写出自己的名字
scene: 你能拼写你的姓吗？Can you spell your surname?
sceneCN: 这里 spell 是「拼写」（第 1 个义项）；句意：你能拼写你的姓吗？

senses.title: To write letters
senses.definition: to write or say the letters of a word in the correct order
senses.definitionCN: 按正确顺序写出或说出单词的字母
senses.example: Can you spell your surname?
senses.exampleCN: 你能拼写你的姓吗？
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of letters in order.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示按顺序排列字母的含义。

senses.title: To say letters aloud
senses.definition: to say the letters of a word one by one
senses.definitionCN: 逐个说出单词的字母
senses.example: The teacher spelled the word aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把这个词逐个字母读了出来。
senses.why: The voice can spell as well as the hand.
senses.whyCN: 嘴和手一样都能拼。

senses.title: To mean trouble
senses.definition: to suggest that something, often bad, will happen
senses.definitionCN: 暗示某事（常为坏事）将会发生
senses.example: Dark clouds spell rain.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云意味着要下雨。
senses.why: Letters that form a word foretell its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拼成词的字母，预告了它的含义。

intro.en: Spell came through French from a Germanic word for a story or saying.
intro.cn: spell 经法语来自日耳曼语中表示故事或说法的词。

items.en: A word for a tale or saying lay behind spell.
items.cn: 表示故事或说法的词是 spell 的源头。

items.en: Espeller meant to tell or recite letters.
items.cn: espeller 意为讲述或读出字母。

items.en: Spell entered English meaning to read letter by letter.
items.cn: spell 以逐字母读出之义进入英语。

items.en: It came to mean writing words correctly.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示正确写出单词。

items.en: To spell trouble used the word for foretelling.
items.cn: spell trouble 借用了预示的含义。

note.en: Spell is compared with look-alike words and verbs of writing and meaning.
note.cn: 把 spell 与形近词以及表示书写和意味的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to look at and understand words

normalIntro.en: To spell is to line letters up until they make a word.
normalIntro.cn: spell 就是把字母排好队，直到成为一个词。

normal.en: Can you spell your surname?
The teacher spelled the word aloud.
normal.cn: 老师把这个词逐个字母读了出来。

normal.en: Dark clouds spell rain.
Please spell out your full name.
He often misspells difficult words.

abstract.en: Letters obey an order or they mean nothing.
abstract.cn: 字母遵守顺序，否则毫无意义。

abstract.en: A name is held together by how it is spelled.
abstract.cn: 一个名字靠它的拼法维系。

abstract.en: To spell is to trust that order creates meaning.
abstract.cn: 拼写，就是相信顺序能创造意义。

examples.en: Can you spell your surname?
examples.cn: 你能拼写你的姓吗？

examples.en: The teacher spelled the word aloud.
examples.cn: 老师把这个词逐个字母读了出来。

examples.en: Dark clouds spell rain.
examples.cn: 乌云意味着要下雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: spell 是「拼写」，也可指「逐字母读出」和「意味着」；spelling 是「拼写、拼法」，misspell 是「拼错」，spell out 是「拼出、明确说明」，spell trouble 是「意味着麻烦」。

root: 来自古法语 espeller，源于日耳曼语中表示讲述、说法的词，核心义为按顺序说出或写出字母，后引申为预示、意味着。

sensesIntro.en: Spell means to write letters in order, to say them aloud, or to mean something bad.
sensesIntro.cn: spell 指按顺序写出字母、逐字母读出，或意味着不好的结果。

core.en: Letters lined up into meaning.
core.cn: 被排成意义的字母。

branches.en: A child writes her name in sand.
branches.cn: 孩子在沙上写出自己的名字。

branches.en: A teacher pronounces each letter slowly.
branches.cn: 老师慢慢读出每个字母。

branches.en: Grey clouds gather over a field.
branches.cn: 灰云在田野上空聚集。

branches.en: Hand and voice both put letters in order.
branches.cn: 手和嘴都把字母按顺序排列。

branches.en: Arranged letters and gathering clouds both announce a meaning.
branches.cn: 排好的字母与聚集的云都在宣告含义。

intro.en: Spell forms nouns and verbs of letters and mistakes.
intro.cn: spell 构成表示字母和错误的动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Spell came through French from Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: spell 经法语来自日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.exampleCN: 他慢慢拼出了自己的名字。

items.example: The word was spelt with two letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个词用了两个字母拼写。

items.meaning: the act or way of spelling
items.example: Check the spelling of the name.

definition_en: to use money to buy things, to pass time in a place or way, or to use up energy
core_image: 收银台上硬币一枚枚被推出去，旁边日历上的日子也一页页翻过
scene: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 spend 是「度过」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他们在海边度过了整个周末。

senses.title: To pay out money
senses.definition: to use money to buy something
senses.definitionCN: 用钱购买东西
senses.example: She spent fifty pounds on the coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了五十英镑买那件大衣。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最常见的含义。

senses.title: To pass time
senses.definition: to pass time in a particular way or place
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式或在特定地点度过时间
senses.example: They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。
senses.why: Time is treated like money that is paid out.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作花出去的钱。

senses.title: To use up energy
senses.definition: to use up energy or effort on something
senses.definitionCN: 在某事上耗尽精力或努力
senses.example: He spent all his energy on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 他把全部精力都花在这个项目上。
senses.why: Energy can be spent like money and time.
senses.whyCN: 精力也能像金钱和时间一样被花掉。

intro.en: Spend came from Latin expendere, to weigh out money, through Old English.
intro.cn: spend 经古英语来自拉丁语 expendere，意为称出钱来支付。

items.en: Expendere meant to weigh out and pay money.
items.cn: expendere 意为称出并支付钱款。

items.en: Spendan meant to pay out or use up.
items.cn: spendan 意为支付或耗尽。

items.en: Spend came to mean passing time as well.
items.cn: spend 也开始表示度过时间。

items.en: Spending became the word for household costs.
items.cn: spending 成为表示家庭开支的词。

items.en: Spend energy extended it beyond money.
items.cn: spend energy 把它扩展到金钱之外。

note.en: Spend is compared with look-alike words and verbs of using resources.
note.cn: 把 spend 与形近词以及表示使用资源的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to go through a period of time

normalIntro.en: To spend is to let something valuable flow out of your hands.
normalIntro.cn: spend 就是让有价值的东西从手中流走。

normal.en: They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
normal.cn: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。

normal.en: She spent fifty pounds on the coat.
normal.cn: 她花了五十英镑买那件大衣。

intro.en: Spring forms irregular verb parts and compounds.
intro.cn: spring 构成不规则动词形式和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Spring has no Latin root; it comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: spring 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语。

items.meaning: to leap or a water source

items.example: The cat has sprung onto the roof.
Deer are springing across the field.
The grass is soft and springy.

items.meaning: a board for jumping or a start
items.example: The job was a springboard to fame.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作是成名的跳板。

definition_zh: 正方形；广场；平方；公正的
definition_en: a shape with four equal sides, an open city space, or fair and honest
core_image: 广场地砖拼成整齐的正方形
scene: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。The children flew kites in the square.
sceneCN: 这里 square 是「广场」（第 2 个义项）；句意：孩子们在广场上放风筝。

senses.title: Four-sided shape
senses.definition: a shape with four equal sides and four right angles
senses.definitionCN: 四条边相等、四个角都是直角的图形
senses.example: She drew a square on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她在黑板上画了一个正方形。
senses.why: This is the concrete shape sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的形状义项。

senses.title: Open city space
senses.definition: an open area in a town, often with buildings around it
senses.definitionCN: 城镇中四周常有建筑的开阔场地
senses.example: The children flew kites in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。
senses.why: The shape became a place in old towns.
senses.whyCN: 在古老城镇里，方形的地块变成了场所。

senses.title: Product of a number
senses.definition: the result of multiplying a number by itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个数自乘所得的结果
senses.example: Five squared is twenty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 五的平方是二十五。
senses.why: A square number is drawn as a square array.
senses.whyCN: 平方数可以排成正方形点阵。

senses.title: Fair and honest
senses.definition: honest and fair in dealing with people
senses.definitionCN: 待人处事诚实公平的
senses.example: It was a square deal for both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双方都是公平的交易。
senses.why: A right angle suggests straight and fair conduct.
senses.whyCN: 直角象征正直、公平的行为。

intro.en: Square comes from Latin exquadrare, to make square, through Old French esquarre.
intro.cn: square 经古法语 esquarre 来自拉丁语 exquadrare，意为使成方形。

items.en: Exquadrare meant to make square.
items.cn: exquadrare 意为使成方形。

items.en: Esquarre meant a square or a rule.
items.cn: esquarre 意为方形或曲尺。

items.en: Square named the shape and the tool.
items.cn: square 既指形状也指工具。

items.en: The open place sense grew in towns.
items.cn: 「广场」义项在城镇中发展起来。

items.en: The fair sense came from honest measure.
items.cn: 「公正」义项来自诚实的度量。

note.en: Square is compared with look-alike words and words for open places.
note.cn: 把 square 与形近词以及表示开阔场地的词作比较。

entries.definition: a shape with four right angles

normalIntro.en: Square is a right-angled shape, a town space, a number, and a fair deal.
normalIntro.cn: square 是直角图形、城镇空地、平方数，也是公平的交易。

normal.en: Fold the paper into a square.
We met in the town square.
Three squared is nine.
They won fair and square.
The room is twelve square metres.
normal.cn: 这个房间有十二平方米。

abstract.en: Equal sides make a steady shape.
abstract.cn: 相等的边构成稳固的图形。

abstract.en: A square deal needs two honest sides.
abstract.cn: 公平的交易需要双方都诚实。

abstract.en: Every number can grow into a square.
abstract.cn: 每个数都能长成自己的平方。

examples.en: She drew a square on the board.
examples.cn: 她在黑板上画了一个正方形。

examples.en: The children flew kites in the square.
examples.cn: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。

examples.en: It was a square deal for both sides.
examples.cn: 这对双方都是公平的交易。

dict_mnemonic.text: square 基本义是「正方形」，由此引申出广场、平方和公正；town square 是城镇广场，square root 是平方根，fair and square 是光明正大。

root: 经古法语 esquarre 来自拉丁语 exquadrare（使成方形），词根 quadr- 表示四；由「四边相等的图形」引申出广场、平方和公正。

sensesIntro.en: Square names a shape, a town space, a product of multiplication, or fair conduct.
sensesIntro.cn: square 指正方形、广场、平方数，或公正的行为。

core.en: Four equal sides meeting at right angles.
core.cn: 四条相等的边以直角相接。

branches.en: A child draws four even lines.
branches.cn: 孩子画出四条等长的线。

branches.en: Paving stones mark a wide open place.
branches.cn: 铺路石围出一片开阔场地。

branches.en: Dots form an even block of rows.
branches.cn: 圆点排成整齐的方阵。

branches.en: A level table suggests an honest deal.
branches.cn: 平稳的桌面象征公平的交易。

branches.en: The shape and the number share one form.
branches.cn: 图形与数字共享同一种形态。

intro.en: Square forms plurals, comparisons, adverbs, and a noun.
intro.cn: square 构成复数、比较级、副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is exquadrare, to make square.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 exquadrare，意为使成方形。

items.example: The board is full of squares.

items.exampleCN: 求一个数的平方很容易。

items.example: This table is squarer than that one.
items.exampleCN: 这张桌子比那张更方正。

items.example: It is the squarest room in the house.
items.exampleCN: 这是屋里最方正的房间。

items.example: The squareness of the box pleased her.

latinEntries.exampleCN: 他们想把石头凿成方形。

definition_en: the people who work for an organization, a strong stick, or the five lines of written music
core_image: 职员们拿着文件走过办公室走廊
scene: 全体员工参加了会议。The whole staff attended the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 staff 是「全体职员」（第 1 个义项）；句意：全体员工参加了会议。

senses.title: Employees
senses.definition: all the people who work for an organization
senses.definitionCN: 为一个机构工作的所有人
senses.example: The whole staff attended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工参加了会议。
senses.why: This is the dominant modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最主要的义项。

senses.title: Walking stick
senses.definition: a long strong stick used for support
senses.definitionCN: 用于支撑身体的长而结实的棍子
senses.example: The old man leaned on his staff.
senses.exampleCN: 老人拄着手杖。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最具体的义项。

senses.title: Musical lines
senses.definition: the set of five lines on which music is written
senses.definitionCN: 书写音乐用的五条平行线
senses.example: The notes stood on the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 音符写在五线谱上。
senses.why: The five lines look like a bundle of sticks.
senses.whyCN: 五条平行线像一束并排的棍子。

intro.en: Staff comes from Old English stæf, a stick or a letter, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: staff 来自古英语 stæf（棍子、字母），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant a stick or post.
items.cn: 该词根意为棍子或柱子。

items.en: Stæf meant a stick and also a letter.
items.cn: stæf 既指棍子，也指字母。

items.en: Staff named a rod of support or office.
items.cn: staff 指支撑用的杖或权杖。

items.en: A staff of office came to mean its holders.
items.cn: 权杖的持有者转指全体职员。

items.en: The five musical lines took the name.
items.cn: 音乐的五条线也采用了这个词。

note.en: Staff is compared with look-alike words and words for workers.
note.cn: 把 staff 与形近词以及表示工作人员的词作比较。

entries.definition: the people employed in a place

normalIntro.en: Staff is a supporting stick that grew into a body of workers and a set of music lines.
normalIntro.cn: staff 原是一根支撑的手杖，后来长出「全体职员」和「五线谱」两义。

normal.en: The staff work hard.
We need more staff.
He walked with a staff.
Notes are written on the staff.
The school staff met today.
normal.cn: 学校教职员工今天开了会。

abstract.en: A stick supports one hand; a staff supports a house.
abstract.cn: 一根杖撑住一只手，一群员工撑起一个机构。

abstract.en: Five lines hold a whole song.
abstract.cn: 五条线，托住一整首歌。

abstract.en: What you lean on becomes what you rely on.
abstract.cn: 你所倚靠之物，终成你所依赖之人。

examples.en: The whole staff attended the meeting.
examples.cn: 全体员工参加了会议。

examples.en: The old man leaned on his staff.
examples.cn: 老人拄着手杖。

examples.en: The notes stood on the staff.
examples.cn: 音符写在五线谱上。

dict_mnemonic.text: staff 是「全体职员」，也指「手杖、五线谱」；teaching staff 是教职员工，staff meeting 是员工会议，staff turnover 是员工流动率。

root: 来自古英语 stæf（棍子、字母），源于日耳曼语词根；由「支撑的杖」转指持杖的官员群体，进而指全体职员，五线谱则取其「并排的条」之意。

sensesIntro.en: Staff means employees, a walking stick, or the five lines of music.
sensesIntro.cn: staff 指全体职员、手杖，或音乐的五线谱。

core.en: A strong stick that supports and holds things together.
core.cn: 一根起支撑作用、把事物维系住的结实棍子。

branches.en: Workers fill the office before nine.
branches.cn: 员工在九点前坐满办公室。

branches.en: A hand grips a tall wooden stick.
branches.cn: 一只手握住高高的木杖。

branches.en: Five lines carry a row of notes.
branches.cn: 五条线承载一排音符。

branches.en: The staff of a house supports its work.
branches.cn: 一个机构的员工支撑起它的运转。

branches.en: Office and orchestra both stand on many lines.
branches.cn: 办公室与乐队，都靠许多条线支撑。

intro.en: Staff forms plurals and a small family of work words.
intro.cn: staff 构成复数以及一组与工作相关的词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 两边的员工在中午会面。
这家诊所人员配备充足。
这里的人员配备是个问题。

definition_en: a raised floor for performing, a period in a process, or to present a play or event
core_image: 灯光亮起，演员走上舞台中央
scene: 演员走上舞台。The actor walked onto the stage.
sceneCN: 这里 stage 是「舞台」（第 1 个义项）；句意：演员走上舞台。

senses.title: Performing platform
senses.definition: a raised floor where actors or musicians perform
senses.definitionCN: 演员或乐手表演用的抬高平台
senses.example: The actor walked onto the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员走上舞台。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的具体义项。

senses.title: Period of a process
senses.definition: a particular point or period in a process
senses.definitionCN: 过程中的某个时刻或时期
senses.example: The project is at an early stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目正处于早期阶段。
senses.why: The platform became a step in time.
senses.whyCN: 「台」的概念延伸为时间上的「台阶」。

senses.title: Put on a show
senses.definition: to arrange and perform a play, concert, or event
senses.definitionCN: 安排并演出戏剧、音乐会或活动
senses.example: They staged a new play last night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们昨晚上演了一出新戏。
senses.why: The verb returns to the theatre sense.
senses.whyCN: 动词义又回到戏剧场景。

intro.en: Stage comes from Latin stare, to stand, through Old French estage, a dwelling or floor.
intro.cn: stage 经古法语 estage（住所、楼层）来自拉丁语 stare（站立）。

items.en: Stare meant to stand.
items.cn: stare 意为站立。

items.en: Estage meant a dwelling or a floor.
items.cn: estage 意为住所或楼层。

items.en: Stage named a raised floor or platform.
items.cn: stage 指抬高的地面或平台。

items.en: The theatre sense became dominant.
items.cn: 戏剧舞台义后来占据主导。

items.en: The time sense grew from step by step.
items.cn: 时间义由「一级一级的台阶」引申而来。

note.en: Stage is compared with look-alike words and words for periods.
note.cn: 把 stage 与形近词以及表示阶段的词作比较。

entries.definition: to act or play for people

normalIntro.en: Stage is a raised floor, a step in time, and the act of putting on a show.
normalIntro.cn: stage 是抬高的台、时间中的一步，也是把戏搬上台的动作。

normal.en: She stood on the stage.
The plan is at an early stage.
He has stage fright.
They staged a concert.
normal.cn: 他们举办了一场音乐会。

normal.en: The singer walked to center stage.

abstract.en: Every life has its stages.
abstract.cn: 每个人生都有自己的阶段。

abstract.en: A step up becomes a stage.
abstract.cn: 抬高一步，就成了舞台。

abstract.en: The world watches what you stage.
abstract.cn: 你搬上台的东西，世界都在看。

examples.en: The actor walked onto the stage.
examples.cn: 演员走上舞台。

examples.en: The project is at an early stage.
examples.cn: 这个项目正处于早期阶段。

examples.en: They staged a new play last night.
examples.cn: 他们昨晚上演了一出新戏。

dict_mnemonic.text: stage 是「舞台、阶段、上演」；on stage 是在台上，stage fright 是怯场，early stage 是早期阶段；过去式加 d 变 staged。

root: 经古法语 estage（住所、楼层）来自拉丁语 stare（站立）；由「抬高的台」引申为舞台，再引申为时间中的一个阶段和上演动作。

sensesIntro.en: Stage means a performing platform, a period in a process, or to put on a show.
sensesIntro.cn: stage 指表演的舞台、过程中的阶段，或上演一出戏。

core.en: A raised place where something is shown.
core.cn: 一个被抬高、用来展示某物的场所。

branches.en: Lights rise on a wooden floor.
branches.cn: 灯光照亮木制台面。

branches.en: A chart marks one point in time.
branches.cn: 图表标出时间中的一个节点。

branches.en: Curtains open and the play begins.
branches.cn: 幕布拉开，戏开始了。

branches.en: A platform and a period are both steps.
branches.cn: 台与阶段，都是「一步」。

branches.en: Each staged event moves through stages.
branches.cn: 每场上演的活动都要经过若干阶段。

intro.en: Stage forms verb parts, adjectives, and theatre compounds.
intro.cn: stage 构成动词变化、形容词和戏剧复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 stare，意为站立。

items.meaning: the act of putting on a show

items.exampleCN: 他的声音听起来很做作。
一名舞台工作人员搬动了椅子。

definition_zh: 站；站立；坐落；忍受；立场；看台
definition_en: to be on the feet, to be located, to endure, or a position on an issue
core_image: 双脚牢牢踩在地上，身体竖直不动
scene: 上课前，班长喊了一声，全班站起来向老师问好。Before class the monitor called out, and the whole class stood up to greet the teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 stand 是「站」（第 1 个义项：双脚立起、身体竖直）；句意：上课前，班长喊了一声，全班站起来向老师问好。

derivatives.zh: 理解，由 under 与 stand 复合

senses.title: To be on the feet
senses.definition: to be upright on the feet
senses.definitionCN: 双脚直立地站着
senses.example: Please stand up.
senses.exampleCN: 请站起来。
senses.why: The feet press into the ground and hold the body upright, so the verb names firm vertical support.
senses.whyCN: 双脚压进地面，把身体撑直，所以这个动词命名的是稳固的竖直支撑。

senses.title: To be located
senses.definition: to be in a particular place or condition
senses.definitionCN: 位于某处或处于某种状态
senses.example: The old tower still stands.
senses.exampleCN: 那座古塔依然矗立着。
senses.why: A building that stays upright on its ground is said to stand there, so the posture of the body describes where things are.
senses.whyCN: 建筑稳稳立在土地上，就被说成 stand 在那里，于是身体的姿态用来描述事物的位置。

senses.title: To endure
senses.definition: to bear something difficult without giving way
senses.definitionCN: 承受困难而不垮掉
senses.example: I can't stand the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 我受不了这噪音。
senses.why: Standing firm under a weight becomes the image of enduring something unpleasant.
senses.whyCN: 在重压之下仍站得住，成了忍受不快之事的画面。

senses.title: A position on an issue
senses.definition: a firm opinion or position that someone takes
senses.definitionCN: 某人采取的坚定看法或位置
senses.example: She took a stand against the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个计划表明了反对立场。
senses.why: A person who will not move from a spot has a position, and that physical firmness becomes a stated opinion.
senses.whyCN: 一个人不肯离开某个位置，就有了立场，而这种身体的坚定变成公开的看法。

senses.title: A stall or viewing area
senses.definition: a raised structure for watching, or a small stall at a market
senses.definitionCN: 观看用的看台，或集市上的小摊
senses.example: We watched the match from the stand.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在看台上看比赛。
senses.why: A structure built to stay in place and hold people becomes a stand, from the same idea of standing firm.
senses.whyCN: 一个固定在那里、承载人群的结构也叫 stand，仍来自「稳稳立住」的观念。

intro.en: Stand is an old Germanic verb of upright posture whose meaning widened to endurance and position.
intro.cn: stand 是古老的日耳曼语直立姿态动词，词义扩展到忍受与立场。

items.en: Standan means to stand or remain upright.
items.cn: standan 意为站立、保持直立。

items.en: The spelling settles as stand and the past form becomes stood.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写定为 stand，过去式成为 stood。

items.en: Stand also means to endure, as in cannot stand.
items.cn: 近代早期，stand 也意为忍受，如 cannot stand。

items.en: A stand becomes a stated position on an issue.
items.cn: 现代英语中，a stand 成为对某事的公开立场。

items.en: A stand also names a market stall or a viewing structure.
items.cn: 现代英语中，stand 还指集市摊位或看台。

note.en: Stand is upright and firm, while sit is settled low and stay is simply remaining.
note.cn: stand 是竖直而稳固，sit 是低处安顿，stay 只是停留。

entries.definition: to move upward to a standing position

normalIntro.en: Stand is the body held upright, and the same firmness becomes endurance and a stated position.
normalIntro.cn: stand 是身体被撑直，同一种稳固又变成忍受与公开立场。

normal.en: Stand up is the common call to rise.
normal.cn: stand up 是叫人起身的常用说法。

normal.en: The past tense is stood, the participle stood.
normal.cn: 过去式是 stood，过去分词也是 stood。

normal.en: A tower stands on a hill means it is located there.
normal.cn: 「a tower stands on a hill」意为塔坐落在那里。

normal.en: Cannot stand means cannot endure.
normal.cn: cannot stand 意为无法忍受。

normal.en: Take a stand means state a firm position.
normal.cn: take a stand 意为表明坚定立场。

abstract.en: Picture two feet pressed firmly into the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚牢牢压在地面上。

abstract.en: See a column holding up a roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一根柱子撑起屋顶。

abstract.en: Think of a flagpole that will not lean.
abstract.cn: 想象一根不肯倾斜的旗杆。

examples.en: Please stand up.
examples.cn: 请站起来。

examples.en: I can't stand the noise.
examples.cn: 我受不了这噪音。

examples.en: The old tower still stands.
examples.cn: 那座古塔依然矗立着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「石坦」——像石头一样坦然地立着，就是站得稳；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 standan，与德语 stehen 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with an upright body, then covers where things stand, what a person can endure, and the position taken.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从竖直的身体开始，继而覆盖事物所在、人能忍受什么，以及所持的立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two feet planted firmly on the ground, the body upright.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚牢牢踩地，身体笔直。

branches.en: The base sense is the body held upright on the feet.
branches.cn: 基本义是身体靠双脚直立。

branches.en: A building staying upright describes where it is.
branches.cn: 建筑保持直立，描述它所在的位置。

branches.en: Standing firm under pressure becomes endurance.
branches.cn: 在压力下站稳就变成忍受。

branches.en: Refusing to move from a spot becomes a stated position.
branches.cn: 不肯离开某个位置就变成公开立场。

branches.en: The upright structure and the viewing stand share the same firm shape.
branches.cn: 直立的结构与看台共享同一种稳固形状。

intro.cn: stand 是本土词干，可构成 understand、withstand、standstill。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in stand; its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: stand 没有拉丁成分，其亲属词属日耳曼语。

items.example: Standan is the Old English ancestor of stand.
items.exampleCN: standan 是 stand 的古英语祖先。

items.example: Stands marks the third person singular.
items.exampleCN: stands 标记第三人称单数。

items.example: Understand means stand in the middle of an idea.
items.exampleCN: understand 原意为站在一个想法之中。
standstill 把 stand 与 still 结合。

definition_en: a rule or measure used to judge quality, a level of quality, or the usual accepted type
core_image: 一把用来衡量长度的尺子
scene: 这家旅馆达到很高的标准。The hotel meets a high standard.
sceneCN: 这里 standard 是「标准」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家旅馆达到很高的标准。

senses.title: Rule for judging
senses.definition: a rule or measure used to judge quality or correctness
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判质量或正确性的规则或尺度
senses.example: The hotel meets a high standard.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆达到很高的标准。
senses.why: A rule for judging quality is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 衡量质量的规则，是这个词的核心义项。

senses.title: Level reached
senses.definition: the level of quality that someone or something reaches
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所达到的质量水平
senses.example: Her work is above the average standard.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作高于一般水准。
senses.why: The measured level grew from the rule itself.
senses.whyCN: 被衡量的水准，由规则本身引申而来。

senses.title: Usual type
senses.definition: of the usual or accepted type, not special
senses.definitionCN: 属于通常或公认类型的，非特殊的
senses.example: This is the standard model.
senses.exampleCN: 这是标准型号。
senses.why: Anything of the accepted type is called standard.
senses.whyCN: 凡属公认类型的事物，都称作标准的。

intro.en: Standard came through Old French from a Germanic compound meaning to stand firmly.
intro.cn: standard 经古法语而来，源头是意为「稳稳站立」的日耳曼语复合词。

items.en: A compound meant standing firmly.
items.cn: 一个复合词意为稳稳站立。

items.en: Estandard named a flag raised as a rallying sign.
items.cn: estandard 指挥舞起来集结人马的旗帜。

items.en: Standard meant a flag and then a fixed measure.
items.cn: standard 先指旗帜，后指固定的度量。

items.en: It named an accepted rule for judging quality.
items.cn: 它指评判质量的公认规则。

items.en: The adjective sense of usual type appeared.
items.cn: 「通常类型」的形容词义随之出现。

note.en: Standard is compared with look-alike words and words for measures of quality.
note.cn: 把 standard 与形近词以及表示质量尺度的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Standard is a rule that measures quality, the level reached, and the usual type.
normalIntro.cn: standard 是衡量质量的规则，是达到的水准，也是常规的类型。

normal.en: The hotel meets a high standard.

normal.en: They set a strict standard for safety.

normal.en: Her work is above the average standard.

normal.en: This is the standard model.
By any standard, the result is good.
normal.cn: 无论按什么标准，结果都不错。

abstract.en: A ruler turns length into a judgement.
abstract.cn: 一把尺子，把长度变成判断。

abstract.en: A level reached becomes a level expected.
abstract.cn: 达到的水准，变成期待的水准。

abstract.en: What most people accept becomes standard.
abstract.cn: 多数人接受的，就成了标准。

root: 经古法语 estandard（军旗）源于日耳曼语「稳稳站立」的复合词；从集结人马的旗帜，引申为公认的度量与评判规则。

sensesIntro.en: Standard means a rule for judging, the level reached, or the usual accepted type.

core.en: A fixed measure for judging.

branches.en: A ruler lies beside the cloth.
branches.cn: 一把尺子放在布料旁。

branches.en: A needle marks the level reached.

branches.en: An ordinary product leaves the factory.

branches.en: The rule and the level it measures belong together.
branches.cn: 规则与它衡量的水准密不可分。

branches.en: The level people expect becomes the usual type.

intro.en: Standard forms verbs and nouns of measuring, and compounds of standing.
intro.cn: standard 构成表示衡量的动词与名词，以及表示站立的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic by way of Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，是经古法语而来的日耳曼语词。

definition_zh: 星；恒星；夜空中的光点；星形符号；明星；主演
definition_en: a self-luminous ball of gas in space, or any bright point in the night sky, or a famous performer, or a star-shaped mark
core_image: 深蓝夜空里一点稳定的亮光，周围其他光点都在轻轻闪烁，只有它像钉子一样钉住
scene: 夜里抬头指着最亮的那一点，你说 That star is brighter than the others.
sceneCN: 这里 star 指「夜空中可见的一个发光点」（第 2 个义项：肉眼所见的天上光点，未必是真恒星）；句意为那颗星比别的都亮。图中可辨识物件：深蓝夜空、一个明显更亮的光点、周围较暗的星点、望远镜。

pos.zh: 星；恒星；光点；星形符号；明星；星级

derivatives.zh: star + -y：多星的；星状的；由本词加形容词后缀
star + -dom：明星地位；后缀表身份或领域
star + -ing：领衔主演的；动词分词作定语

senses.title: A self-luminous ball of gas
senses.titleCN: 自身发光的巨大气体球：恒星
senses.definition: a massive ball of gas that shines by nuclear fusion, such as the sun
senses.definitionCN: 靠核聚变发光的大型气体球，如太阳
senses.example: The sun is an ordinary star in an ordinary galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳只是普通星系中一颗普通的恒星。
senses.why: the modern astronomical sense is narrow: only a body that makes its own light counts, which is why the sun is a star and the moon is not.
senses.whyCN: 现代天文学义很窄：只有自己发光的才算法，因此太阳是恒星而月亮不是。

senses.title: A bright point in the night sky
senses.titleCN: 夜空中肉眼可见的光点
senses.definition: any luminous point seen in the night sky, whether a true star, a planet or a distant sun
senses.definitionCN: 夜空中任何可见的亮点，无论真恒星、行星还是遥远的太阳
senses.example: That star is brighter than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗星比别的都亮。
senses.why: before telescopes, every point of light looked alike, so the everyday sense keeps the older, wider meaning that includes planets.
senses.whyCN: 在望远镜之前，所有光点看起来都一样，因此日常义保留了包含行星的较宽旧义。

senses.title: A star-shaped mark
senses.titleCN: 星形符号；星号状的记号
senses.definition: a mark or symbol with radiating points, used in printing, grading or decoration
senses.definitionCN: 带放射状尖角的符号，用于印刷、评级或装饰
senses.example: A star beside the title marks a revised edition.
senses.exampleCN: 标题旁的星号表示修订版。
senses.why: the shape sense is very old: a drawn star is a simplified picture of the radiating light, and the mark keeps that picture.
senses.whyCN: 形状义很古老：画出来的星是对放射光芒的简化图示，符号保留的正是这幅图。

senses.title: A famous performer
senses.titleCN: 明星：出名的演员或表演者
senses.definition: a very famous actor, singer or athlete
senses.definitionCN: 非常出名的演员、歌手或运动员
senses.example: She became a star before she turned twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十岁前就成了明星。
senses.why: theatre slang of the nineteenth century borrowed the sky image: the star is the one point everyone in the audience looks at.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的剧场俚语借用了天上的意象：明星就是全场观众都看的那一点。

senses.title: To play the leading role
senses.definition: to appear as the leading performer in a film or play
senses.definitionCN: 在电影或戏剧中担任主要表演者
senses.example: He starred in three films that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年他主演了三部电影。
senses.why: the verb is the celebrity noun turned into an action: to star is to be the point the production is built around.
senses.whyCN: 动词是明星名词的动作化：to star 就是成为整部作品围绕的那一点。

senses.title: A rating symbol
senses.titleCN: 星级：用星数表示质量的记号
senses.definition: a symbol used in sets to grade quality, as in a five-star rating
senses.definitionCN: 成组使用、以星数表示质量等级的符号
senses.example: The restaurant earned a third star this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅今年拿到了第三颗星。
senses.why: a countable mark makes quality countable, so hotels and restaurants were ranked in stars rather than in words.
senses.whyCN: 可数的符号让质量也可数，于是旅馆与餐厅用星数而非文字来分级。

senses.title: Destiny fixed in the sky
senses.titleCN: 命数：被认为写在天上的命运
senses.definition: a person's fate, imagined as determined by the position of the stars at birth
senses.definitionCN: 被认为由出生时星位决定的个人命运
senses.example: Their meeting seemed written in the stars.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的相遇像是命中注定。
senses.why: astrology read the sky as a text, so the plural the stars came to mean the written fate rather than the bodies themselves.
senses.whyCN: 占星把天空当作文本，于是复数 the stars 转而指写好的命数，而非天体本身。

senses.title: The main attraction
senses.titleCN: 展览或演出中最吸引人的那一个
senses.definition: the person or object that a show or exhibition is built around
senses.definitionCN: 演出或展览围绕其展开的人或物
senses.example: The manuscript is the star of the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿是整批藏品中的明星。
senses.why: the metaphor extends from people to objects: whatever the crowd comes for is the star, even if it is a fossil.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻从人扩展到物：人群为之而来的那一个就是明星，哪怕它是一块化石。

intro.en: Star is native English, from Old English steorra, and has no Latin source; its Latin and Greek relatives are cognates from the same reconstructed Indo-European root. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: star 是英语本族词，来自古英语 steorra，并非拉丁来源；它的拉丁与希腊同族词出自同一印欧重构词根，属同源而非派生。年代均为约数。

items.en: Steorra is the Old English noun for a star, recorded before the Norman conquest and unchanged in meaning.
items.cn: steorra 是古英语的「星」，诺曼征服之前已有记录，意义未变。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic set that includes Old High German sterro and Gothic stairno, all pointing to a common Germanic form.
items.cn: 这个词属于一个日耳曼词集，包括古高地德语 sterro 与哥特语 stairno，都指向一个共同的日耳曼形式。

items.en: Latin stella and Greek aster are cognates, not sources: all these forms descend from a reconstructed Indo-European root commonly written *ster-, a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: 拉丁 stella 与希腊 aster 是同源词，而非来源：这些形式都出自一个通常写作 *ster- 的印欧重构词根，那是重构而非有书证的原词。

items.en: Once it was shown that the sun is itself a star, the technical sense narrowed to a self-luminous body, while everyday speech kept the wider sense of any point of light.
items.cn: 在确认太阳本身是一颗恒星之后，术语义收窄为自身发光的天体，而日常说法仍保留「任何光点」的宽义。

items.en: The theatrical use of star for the leading performer is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when playbills began to set the favourite's name in large type.
items.cn: 一般认为，star 指领衔演员的剧场用法始于 19 世纪，当时海报开始把最受欢迎者的名字排成大号字。

items.en: Root uncertainty: the Indo-European root *ster- is a reconstruction, and its deeper shape is debated. First-date uncertainty only: the first use of star for a celebrity is not exactly dated and is usually placed somewhere in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 词根存疑：印欧词根 *ster- 属重构形式，其更早形态仍有争论。仅首见年代存疑：star 指明星的最早用例没有确切年代，通常笼统定在 19 世纪。

note.en: Group one holds sky objects and words that look like relatives; group two holds the everyday near-equivalents of the fame and mark senses.
note.cn: 第一组是天体以及看起来像同族的词；第二组是「名声」与「符号」两个义项的近义说法。

entries.definition: A planet orbits a star and shines only by reflected light; Greek planētēs meant 'wanderer', because planets drift against the fixed stars.
entries.definitionCN: 行星绕恒星运行，只反射光；希腊 planētēs 意为「漫游者」，因为行星在恒星间移动。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of stars', borrowed from Latin stella; it never replaces the noun star in ordinary use.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「恒星的」形容词，借自拉丁 stella；日常使用中不能替代名词 star。

entries.definition: From Greek asteriskos 'little star', a diminutive of aster; it names the typed symbol rather than a celestial body.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 asteriskos「小星」，是 aster 的指小形式；它指打字符号而非天体。

entries.tag: fame itself or a famous person
entries.definition: A neutral, often journalistic word for fame and the famous; star adds the image of being the point everyone watches.
entries.definitionCN: 对名声与名人的中性、常为新闻体的说法；star 多了「众人目光汇聚之点」的意象。

entries.definition: The proper name of the star nearest to us; astronomy says the sun is a star, but the two words are not interchangeable in idiom.
entries.definitionCN: 离我们最近的恒星的名字；天文学说太阳是恒星，但两个词在惯用语中不能互换。

entries.tag: a rocky body, star-like in shape
entries.definition: Greek astēr 'star' plus -oeidēs 'like': it means star-like in appearance, not a star, and names a small rocky body.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊 astēr「星」加 -oeidēs「像」：意为外形像星，并非恒星，指小岩石天体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One sky word, three lives: a sun, a famous face, a typed mark.
normal.cn: 一个天空词，三种活法：恒星、名人、打出的符号。

normal.en: The family runs starry, stardom, starlight, starless.
Stars are graded: a five-star hotel.
normal.cn: 星级可以计数：五星级旅馆。

normal.en: The verb takes the same form: he stars in the film.
normal.cn: 动词同形：他主演这部电影。

normal.en: Latin stella and Greek aster are cousins, not parents.
normal.cn: 拉丁 stella 与希腊 aster 是表亲，不是父母。

abstract.en: Picture one nail holding a whole map of glittering pins in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚钉子把满图闪亮的针都固定在原位。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre where every light is turned off except one.
abstract.cn: 想象一座剧院，所有灯都关掉，只剩一盏。

abstract.en: Picture a small drawn star stamped on a page to mean quality.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页上盖着一枚手绘小星，用来表示品质。

examples.en: The brightest star in the sky is Sirius.
examples.cn: 夜空中最亮的恒星是天狼星。

examples.en: She starred in a documentary about the reef.
examples.cn: 她主演了一部关于珊瑚礁的纪录片。

examples.en: The guide gave the trail a two-star difficulty rating.
examples.cn: 指南把这条步道评为两星难度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「star」读音像「是他」——夜空中最亮的那点「就是他」 → 星；引申为明星

root: 古英语 steorra「星」，属日耳曼本族词；与拉丁 stella、希腊 aster 同出印欧重构词根 *ster-（重构形式，非派生关系）；「明星」义一般认为始于 19 世纪剧场用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: a single point that everyone can see, and that point is then a burning sun, a night light, a drawn mark, a famous face, a leading role, a quality grade, a written fate and the main attraction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：一个所有人都看得见的点；这个点依次是燃烧的太阳、夜空的光、画出的符号、成名的面孔、领衔的角色、质量的等级、写好的命数、最吸引人的展品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one steady point of light among many flickering ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多闪烁光点中一个稳定的亮点。

branches.en: LIGHT IN THE SKY: the astronomical body and the everyday point of light.
branches.cn: 天上的光：天文学上的恒星与日常所见的光点。

branches.en: DRAWN MARKS: the radiating shape and the countable grade.
branches.cn: 画出的记号：放射状图形与可数的等级。

branches.en: THE WATCHED PERSON: fame and the leading role it brings.
branches.cn: 被注视的人：名声与随之而来的主角位置。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN SKY: fate read in the positions of stars.
branches.cn: 写好的天空：从星位读出的命数。

branches.en: THE MAIN THING: any object a whole exhibition is built around.
branches.cn: 最主要的那一个：整场展览围绕的任何物件。

intro.en: Star is a free native English root that takes ordinary Germanic suffixes; its Latin and Greek cousins are stella and aster, which supply the borrowed adjectives.
intro.cn: star 是英语本族的自由词根，接普通日耳曼后缀；它的拉丁与希腊表亲 stella、aster 提供借入的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stella supplies stellar, constellation and stellify; Greek aster supplies asterisk, asteroid and asterism. None of them derives from English star.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stella 提供 stellar、constellation、stellify；希腊 aster 提供 asterisk、asteroid、asterism。它们都不是由英语 star 派生。

items.example: The root is free and takes native suffixes.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是自由的，可接本族后缀。

items.example: Stardom is the state of being a star.
items.exampleCN: stardom 是明星的身份状态。

items.example: A starless night has no visible stars.
items.exampleCN: starless night 指看不见星的夜。

items.example: A Latin cognate, not the source of star.
items.exampleCN: 这是拉丁同源词，不是 star 的来源。

items.example: Greek aster feeds asterisk and asteroid.
items.exampleCN: 希腊 aster 衍生 asterisk 与 asteroid。

items.example: Latin built the noun from stella.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用 stella 造出这个名词。

latinEntries.structure: astrum, astri (n., second declension; from Greek astron)

definition_en: to begin doing something, to set out on a journey, or to make a machine begin working
core_image: 发令枪响，选手冲出去
scene: 会议九点开始。The meeting starts at nine.
sceneCN: 这里 start 是「开始」（第 1 个义项）；句意：会议九点开始。

senses.title: Begin an action
senses.definition: to begin doing something
senses.definitionCN: 着手做某事
senses.example: The meeting starts at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 会议九点开始。
senses.why: Beginning an action is the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 开始一个动作，是这个词的中心义项。

senses.title: Set out
senses.definition: to leave a place and begin a journey
senses.definitionCN: 离开某地并开始一段旅程
senses.example: We started for the airport at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 我们黎明时出发去机场。
senses.why: Setting out is beginning a journey.
senses.whyCN: 出发，就是开始一段旅程。

senses.title: Make it run
senses.definition: to make a machine or engine begin working
senses.definitionCN: 使机器或发动机开始运转
senses.example: The car won't start in cold weather.

senses.why: Making a machine run is beginning its motion.
senses.whyCN: 让机器运转，就是开始它的运动。

intro.en: Start comes from Old English styrtan, to leap up, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: start 来自古英语 styrtan（跳起），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root described a sudden jump.
items.cn: 该词根描述突然的一跳。

items.en: Styrtan meant to leap up.
items.cn: styrtan 意为跳起。

items.en: Start meant to move suddenly.
items.cn: start 意为猛然移动。

items.en: It came to mean beginning a journey or action.
items.cn: 它转而表示开始旅程或行动。

items.en: A machine sense of beginning to run grew.
items.cn: 「机器开始运转」的义项发展起来。

note.en: Start is compared with look-alike words and words for beginning.
note.cn: 把 start 与形近词以及表示开始的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Start is to begin, to set out, or to make something run.
normalIntro.cn: start 是开始、出发，或让某物运转起来。

normal.en: The meeting starts at nine.
We started for the airport at dawn.
normal.cn: 我们黎明时出发去机场。

normal.en: The car won't start in cold weather.
normal.cn: 天冷时这辆车启动不了。

normal.en: She started a small business.
A good start makes the rest easier.
normal.cn: 良好的开端让后面更容易。

abstract.en: Every road begins at the first step.
abstract.cn: 每条路都从第一步开始。

abstract.en: To start is to choose one direction.
abstract.cn: 开始，就是选定一个方向。

abstract.en: The engine turns, and the journey exists.
abstract.cn: 引擎一转，旅程才存在。

examples.en: The meeting starts at nine.
examples.cn: 会议九点开始。

examples.en: We started for the airport at dawn.
examples.cn: 我们黎明时出发去机场。

examples.en: The car won't start in cold weather.
examples.cn: 天冷时这辆车启动不了。

dict_mnemonic.text: start 是「开始」，也是「出发」和「启动」；from the start 是从一开始，start up 是启动或开办，starter 是启动器。

root: 来自古英语 styrtan（跳起），源于日耳曼语词根；由猛然一跳，引申为动身出发、开始行动，再到机器开始运转。

sensesIntro.en: Start means to begin something, to set out, or to make an engine run.
sensesIntro.cn: start 指开始某事、动身出发，或启动发动机。

core.en: A sudden move that sets things going.
core.cn: 发起动作的那一下猛然移动。

branches.en: A runner waits for the gun.
branches.cn: 选手等待发令枪。

branches.en: A traveller leaves at dawn.
branches.cn: 旅人黎明时动身。

branches.en: A key turns in the ignition.
branches.cn: 钥匙在点火处转动。

branches.en: The race and the journey both begin with a first move.
branches.cn: 比赛与旅程，都从第一步开始。

branches.en: An action and an engine both need a trigger.
branches.cn: 行动与引擎，都需要一个触发。

intro.en: Start forms verb parts and nouns of beginning and setting out.
intro.cn: start 构成动词变化，以及表示开始与出发的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: a thing that starts, or a first course
a new company or the act of starting
items.exampleCN: 这家初创公司发展很快。
